Mattenai
MAT-ten-eye
n. (proper, men of the restoration; Hebrew, liberal or a gift of the LORD)
Hebrew Mattenay, from mattan, a gift — liberal, or gift of Jehovah. Three men bear it, two in Ezra's register of those who put away strange wives and one among the priests in Nehemiah.

Biblical Definition

Two of the name stand in the register of Ezra 10, a chapter that names every man who had taken a strange wife and separated from her: “Of the sons of Hashum; Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei” (Ezra 10:33), and “Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau” (Ezra 10:37). A third is a priest in the days of Joiakim: “And of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi” (Nehemiah 12:19). The two books are the record of the same generation at two stages: the men whose repentance was written down in Ezra, and the courses of priests serving in an ordered house in Nehemiah. A name meaning gift stands on both lists, and the second could not have existed without the first.

Origin & Era

Webster (1828) has no entry for this proper name; Scripture fixes it as the name of two men in the register of Ezra 10 and of a priest in Nehemiah 12.

expand to see more

GIFT, n. A present; any thing given or bestowed; an offering or donation.

LIBERAL, a. Generous; bountiful; munificent; not selfish, narrow or contracted in mind.

COURSE, n. Order of succession; particularly, the order in which the priests ministered in the temple by turns.

CONFESSION, n. Acknowledgment of a fault; a public avowal of sin or of faith.

ORDER, n. Regular disposition or methodical arrangement of things; a state in which things bear a due relation to each other.

Key Scripture

Ezra 10:33 — "Of the sons of Hashum; Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei."

Ezra 10:37 — "Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau,"

Nehemiah 12:19 — "And of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;"

Ezra 10:1 — "Now when Ezra had prayed, and when he had confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, there assembled unto him out of Israel a very great congregation of men and women and children: for the people wept very sore."

Modern Corruption

Public confession of sin is regarded as needlessly humiliating and best kept private, and Ezra 10 is a whole chapter of names — the biblical precedent for a repentance that is owned openly where the sin was open.

expand to see more

Ezra 10 does something no modern institution would do: it names them. Man after man, family after family, the men who had married strange wives are listed in the word of God, and Mattenai is twice among them. The instinct to keep such things private is not wholly wrong — Scripture guards reputations, forbids talebearing, and orders private sin to be dealt with privately, beginning with a word between two. But where the sin was public and the whole congregation was affected, the repentance was public too, and the chapter opens with Ezra weeping and casting himself down before the house of God, with a very great congregation of men, women and children weeping with him.

What came of it is in Nehemiah. The generation whose failures are listed in Ezra 10 is the generation whose priests are listed by course in Nehemiah 12, serving an ordered house with the wall built and the law read. Repentance recorded in one book and service recorded in the next. The order of those two chapters is the pastoral point: God does not restore a people around their sin, and he does restore a people who have dealt with it.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Mattenay (H4982), liberal; mattan (H4976), a gift; nathan (H5414), to give; machlaqah (H4256), a course or division.

expand to see more

Hebrew Mattenay (H4982) — Mattenai; liberal, or a gift of Jehovah.

Hebrew mattan (H4976) — a gift, a present; the root of the name.

Hebrew nathan (H5414) — to give; the verb behind a whole family of Hebrew names.

Hebrew machlaqah (H4256) — a division, a course; the priestly rotations of Nehemiah 12.

Hebrew yadah (H3034) — to confess; the act Ezra required of the assembly.

Usage

"“Of the sons of Hashum; Mattenai” — in the register of repentance."

"“Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasau” — a second man of the name."

"“And of Joiarib, Mattenai” — a priest in an ordered house."
